rationale: THE `exports` CONTRACT for PHP — a name the file PUBLISHES and no declaration in it writes. This lane had RULED the type inapplicable on a measured parse-tree count, and the ruling was falsified by its own probe: the `define('NAME', …)` test compared `arguments.namedChild(0)` against `string`/`encapsed_string` while tree-sitter-php puts an `argument` node between them, so the rule could not fire on any input, and no corpus could make it non-zero. The control corpus (validation/m14/fixtures/php/exports-probe-controls.mts) reads 1 on `define("X", 1);` where the corpus sweep read 0; with the wrapper descended the corpus reads 60 occurrences in 20 files, 49 of them at file scope. So `exports` is a GAP, implemented here, and the corpus numbers in docs/analyzers/php.md are the post-fix ones. THREE rules, each load-bearing for the counts: (1) the callee is EXACTLY the bare name `define` — the qualified `class_alias` in this fixture is a different function and is refused; (2) the first argument's VALUE is a string literal read THROUGH the `argument` wrapper — `define($name, 4)` publishes a name nobody can write down, so no edge may be invented for it, and refusing it is what keeps the endpoint set resolvable; (3) the call is at FILE scope — `define('LAZY_ONLY', 3)` sits in a function body, so the FILE does not publish it and an edge from `global` would assert something the file does not guarantee. Rule 3's asymmetry is why this is a fixture and not a count: `define('CONDITIONAL_TOP_LEVEL', 2)` is inside a top-level `if`, which is NOT a scope — it executes when the file is included — so it IS published. Getting that backwards would silently drop real publications. The symbol span is pinned to the NAME inside the quotes, matching the `const_declaration` branch's convention for the same kind. The global-vs-namespace contrast is pinned too: `DECLARED_CONST` is namespace-scoped and carried by `contains`, a `define()`d name resolves against the GLOBAL scope and gets no ownerName and therefore no `contains` edge — conflating the two is the mislabelling this fixture exists to catch. RULE 1 WAS WRONG AND IS NOW A RESOLUTION RULE (2026-10-08): the callee must resolve to the global `define`, which the bare name reaches only through PHP's UNQUALIFIED-name fallback, while the fully qualified `\define` reaches it unconditionally ("Fully qualified names always resolve to the name without leading namespace separator"). A whole-population define-audit built the denominator this contract never had — every `define`-family call in the admitted population, split by callee resolution, scope and name literalness — and read 58 tree-implied file-scope publications against 57 emitted edges. The missing one was phpunit's `tests/end-to-end/generic/_files/auto_prepend_file.php`: one file-scope `\define('AUTO_PREPEND_FILE_LOADED', true);`, a file whose ENTIRE PURPOSE is that a prepended file publishes a constant later scripts read, refused for its spelling alone. The audit also priced the three shapes the rule still refuses — qualified `Other\define` (a different function), relative `namespace\define` (no global fallback: the fallback is a rule for unqualified names) and the aliased `use function define as pub` (which DOES publish, and occurs 0 times in 5,094 files, so it is recorded rather than half-implemented) — and measured 0 files that declare their own `define`, the one unsoundness the bare-name test could have had.

forbidSymbols.name: LAZY_ONLY
forbidSymbols.note: a `define()` inside a function body publishes the name only if that function runs; the file does not publish it, so neither the symbol nor the edge may exist

forbidSymbols.name: NAMESPACED_OTHER
forbidSymbols.note: a QUALIFIED callee (`Other\define`) is a different function; it publishes nothing, so no symbol may be invented for its first argument

forbidSymbols.name: RELATIVE_NAMESPACE_SHAPE
forbidSymbols.note: a RELATIVE callee (`namespace\define`) resolves to the current namespace and does not fall back to the global function, so nothing is published

forbidSymbols.name: NESTED_ABSOLUTE
forbidSymbols.note: the scope rule is independent of the callee's spelling: a `\define` inside a function body is still a nested call, and the file does not publish it

forbidSymbols.name: ALIASED_PUBLICATION
forbidSymbols.note: `pub('X', 1)` through `use function define as pub;` DOES publish in PHP (unqualified names go through the function import table), but the shape is PRICED at 0 occurrences over the whole admitted population by exports-probe.mts, so the lane refuses it and records the reason rather than half-implementing an import table for one callee

expectRelationships.note: the FULLY QUALIFIED spelling of the global `define`. PHP resolves `\define` to the global function unconditionally (no namespace lookup, no fallback), so refusing this callee was a MISSED publication — measured: phpunit's `tests/end-to-end/generic/_files/auto_prepend_file.php` is one file-scope `\define('AUTO_PREPEND_FILE_LOADED', true);` whose whole purpose is a globally visible constant, and the census went 57 -> 58 `exports` edges when this shape was accepted.
a top-level `if` is not a scope: this call runs when the file is included, so the file DOES publish the name

forbidRelationships.note: the scope rule: a `define()` in a function body is not a file publication. Emitting it would put 11 corpus edges (measured) on a claim the file does not make.
the callee rule: a QUALIFIED `class_alias(...)` is a different function. The bare-name rule is what keeps a same-named user function from being read as the builtin.
an alias publishes the NEW name, never the class it points at; the target must be the name a consumer writes.
rule R7: no empty endpoint. `define($name, 4)` has no literal name, and the 1 corpus occurrence of that shape must stay unemitted rather than be given an invented target.

the label rule: a `define()`d name resolves against the GLOBAL scope, so it has no owner and gets NO `contains` edge. `contains` is the edge for a name something in the file declares — publishing one is `exports`, and filing it under both is how a file appears to contain a global.
same: no ownerName, therefore no contains edge

the QUALIFIED-callee rule. `Other\define(...)` resolves against the current namespace, so it is a userland function with that name; emitting an edge from it would assert a publication PHP never performs.

the RELATIVE-callee rule, and the reason the fixture spells both of them: `namespace\define(...)` differs from the emitted bare form by five characters and resolves to `App\Config\define` WITHOUT the global fallback (the fallback is a rule for unqualified names only). A rule that widened to `endsWith('define')` would publish this and phpunit's class_alias-free corpus would never notice.
the scope rule must apply to the new absolute shape too — the fix must not arrive with a loophole for it

an aliased `define` publishes in PHP, and this lane refuses it on a MEASURED population of 0 (`aliased-use-function` occurrences over 5,094 admitted files, exports-probe.mts). Recorded as a priced boundary rather than silently unimplemented.

forbidExports.name: LAZY_ONLY
forbidExports.note: same scope rule, on the ExportInfo channel as well as the relationship — the two must not disagree

forbidExports.name: NAMESPACED_OTHER
forbidExports.note: the ExportInfo channel must refuse a qualified callee exactly as the relationship channel does

forbidExports.name: RELATIVE_NAMESPACE_SHAPE
forbidExports.note: the ExportInfo channel must refuse a relative callee too

forbidExports.name: NESTED_ABSOLUTE
forbidExports.note: and must refuse the absolute spelling when the call is nested

forbidExports.name: ALIASED_PUBLICATION
forbidExports.note: priced at 0 occurrences over the admitted population — refused on the ExportInfo channel for the same reason, so the two channels cannot disagree
